unchanged.

night.

He lives at home with son and wife, his son notes he found a 
pack of cigs a few weeks ago that was missing 6 cigs (son feels 
pt was smoking though the pt denies).

Son also notes the pt has 
been trying to follow a low sodium / fluid restricted diet, but

Brief Hospital ___ #1:

Intially was 
diuresed, and given standing ipratropium nebs.

He had per the 
son started smoking again, and the negative impacts of smoking 
on all aspects of his health was stressed with the patient.

It 
was decided to pursue TEE/DCCV, with the premise that atrial 
kick would improve forward flow and decrease his rather high 
rate of decompensated heart failure admissions.
CCU ___:

On the day of transfer, patient was cardioverted with TEE, as it 
was felt that patient's poor forward flow might be improved with 
sinus rhythm.

Post cardioversion he was noted to be hypotensive 
and bradycardic with what appeared to be a junctional rhythm.
He was started on a dopamine gtt and transferred to the CCU.

His 
carvedilol, amiodarone and diltiazem were held.
His pressure and

HR improved and he was weaned off of dopamine and transferred 
back to ___.
Patient came back with SBPs in 120s, HR in ___, on 2L with sats
2L qhs).

Diuresis was continued with BID lasix 80mg IV, and BID 
electrolytes.

His blood pressures remained in the 110s-120s 
systolic with HR in ___ for 36-48 hours post DCCV.

Overnight ___, his pressures began to increase, as did his 
heart rate.

Carvedilol was added as the BP and HR tolerated, 
and Valsartan was added as the BP allowed.

Spironolactone was 
also added given the degree of heart failure.

He was strongly encouraged not to smoke, and to 
limit his salt and water intake.

This was stressed multiple 
times to him and his family.
